At least 10 people were killed in clashes between security forces and artisanal gold miners in Guinea’s Siguiri region on Wednesday, according to the Guinean government. The violence marks a further escalation in a crackdown that has forced thousands of West African workers into neighbouring Mali.

Since Guinea banned unauthorised gold mining in Siguiri on 2 November, Mali has recorded approximately 160,000 arrivals, including 100,000 in Bamako and 60,000 in the border town of Kourémalé.

Malian authorities separately reported 10 deaths among those expelled by 11 November. The World Health Organization says more than 60,000 people have been assisted to return to their countries of origin, but overcrowding, inadequate shelter and limited access to safe water and sanitation continue to pose serious humanitarian risks.
